awd_titl_txt: NSF Mechanics of Materials and Structures Grantee Meeting at the 2025 Society of Engineering Science (SES) Annual Technical Meeting; Atlanta, Georgia; 12-15 October 2025
awd_abstract_narration:
This grant provides travel support for Principal Investigators (PIs) with current active awards from the NSF Mechanics of Materials and Structures (MoMS) program to attend the 2025 MoMS Grantee Meeting, an integral part of the Society of Engineering Science (SES) Annual Technical Meeting. Scheduled for 12-15 October 2025, in Atlanta, Georgia, the meeting will serve as a platform to bring together NSF MoMS grantees, offering opportunities to strengthen collaborations and facilitate the exchange of cutting-edge ideas and research findings. The meeting will feature a series of poster sessions where grantees can present their research, encouraging peer review, feedback, and discussion. Panel discussions, led by invited experts, will dive deep into current challenges and opportunities in the field of mechanics of materials and structures. Topics will include advances in structural and soft materials, new insights into metamaterials, and the use of data-driven approaches to tackle complex engineering problems. The meeting will also include various social activities designed to promote networking and foster potential collaborations across disciplines and institutions.

SES has long been a catalyst for advancing research in mechanics, particularly in the areas of structural materials, soft materials, and metamaterials. By providing a forum for the exchange of ideas between seasoned researchers and emerging talent, the meeting will help drive forward-thinking discussions and innovative solutions to pressing challenges in the field. The event will also offer invaluable mentorship opportunities, where established PIs can share insights on how to navigate the research landscape, secure NSF funding, and develop competitive proposals. The 2025 MoMS Grantee Meeting aims to further solidify the mechanics of materials and structures community by strengthening its connections and providing the next generation of researchers with the tools and guidance needed to thrive in their academic and professional careers. This gathering will foster an environment of collaboration and innovation, propelling forward research that is critical to advancing the mechanics of materials and structures, as well as addressing emerging global challenges.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
The NSF Mechanics of Materials and Structures (MoMS) Grantee Meeting was successfully held during the 2025 Society of Engineering Science (SES) Annual Technical Meeting in Atlanta, Georgia. The meeting brought together approximately 130 researchers from universities across the United States who are supported by the National Science Foundation's MoMS program. Its goal was to strengthen the national research community by providing opportunities to share scientific discoveries, discuss emerging challenges, and establish new collaborations.

A major highlight of the meeting was a panel discussion titled "How Can Mechanics Survive and Thrive in the AI Era?" The panel brought together leading researchers to discuss how advances in artificial intelligence are changing engineering research and how data-driven methods can be integrated with the fundamental principles of mechanics. The discussion emphasized that while artificial intelligence offers powerful new tools for scientific discovery, advances in engineering continue to rely on a deep understanding of the physical laws that govern material and structural behavior.

The meeting also featured two poster sessions with 127 research presentations from investigators supported by the NSF MoMS program. These presentations showcased a wide range of research topics, including advanced structural materials, soft materials, metamaterials, manufacturing, biomechanics, computational modeling, and artificial intelligence for engineering applications. The poster sessions encouraged in-depth scientific discussions and provided participants with opportunities to exchange ideas, receive feedback, and identify future research collaborations.

Beyond presenting research results, the meeting strengthened connections within the mechanics community. PIs from different universities and disciplines were able to share expertise, discuss common scientific challenges, and develop new partnerships that are expected to lead to future collaborative research projects. By bringing together researchers with complementary backgrounds, the meeting helped promote interdisciplinary approaches to solving complex engineering problems.

The meeting also provided valuable professional development opportunities, particularly for early-career faculty and researchers. Participants interacted with established leaders in the field, learned about emerging research directions, and expanded their professional networks. These interactions help build a strong and diverse future workforce in engineering research and education.

Overall, this award successfully created a national forum for scientific exchange within the mechanics of materials and structures community. By fostering collaboration, encouraging discussions on emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, and strengthening professional networks among researchers, the meeting advanced the exchange of knowledge and supported future innovation in engineering science. The collaborations and ideas generated during the meeting are expected to contribute to future advances in materials, manufacturing, infrastructure, energy technologies, and biomedical engineering, while helping maintain U.S. leadership in mechanics research.
